mathy1551.title: Renwick, Abstracts of Protocols of Town Clerks of Glasgow,vol1,protocol71
mathy1551.reading: 3 February 1550/51: John Hawstoune, son and heir of late Thomas Hawstoune, citizen, sells a barn at Powdrait to David Mathy and Mergaret Androsoune, expressly his spouse, and their lawful heirs. Boundaries: Peter Adam west, James Hyndschaw east, street north, Malindin or burn south.

mathy1554.title: Renwick, Abstracts of Protocols,vol1,protocols183–184
mathy1554.reading: 10 May 1554: David Mathy and Robert Glesgw are expressly comburgesses among witnesses to John Androsoune’s sasine as heir of father Patrick. Protocol184 is the same-day act with the same witnesses. No Mathy/Glesgw kinship clause.

mathy1554b.title: Renwick, Abstracts of Protocols,vol1,protocol189
mathy1554b.reading: 4 July 1554: David Mathy witnesses the transaction involving Beatrix Stark and John Stene, heir of Richard Allane. The witness is alive on this date; joining him to the 1550/51 purchaser remains probable.

bridge1582.title: Renwick, Abstracts of Protocols,vol8,protocol2370

companion_subject.wikitext:
== Biography ==
Mergaret Androsoune was expressly described as the spouse of David Mathy when the couple bought a barn at Powdrait, Glasgow, from John Hawstoune on 3 February 1550/51.<ref>Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol.1, protocol71, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsofproto01glas/page/n60/mode/1up p.27]; page image inspected 30 September 2026. Printed abstract; underlying protocol manuscript uninspected.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
The record names the spouses and their lawful heirs collectively; it does not identify any children or parents. It gives no birth or death date. [[Anderson-3241|Margaret Anderson]] is a sparse compatible candidate, not a proved match. Her unsupported John Kelman spouse does not establish a conflict. The David Mathy burgess witness in 1554 is probably the same husband by name and city, but the later acts do not name Mergaret. Keep the household and profile identity qualifications explicit.
